sets.relationshipLabel: a container and the small thing kept in it
sets.explanation: A jar holds a loose button and a spool holds wound thread — each pair names a keeper and the small item it stores.

sets.relationshipLabel: the tool that lets the other tool/thing work
sets.explanation: A thimble lets you push a needle safely, just as a buttonhook lets you fasten a boot — the first tool exists to enable the second.

sets.relationshipLabel: the earlier and later state of decline
sets.explanation: Loose leads to missing and new leads to outgrown — each pair tracks an intact state sliding into a diminished one.

sets.relationshipLabel: a fastener and the one feature it can never have
sets.explanation: A snap never has a buttonhole and a zipper never has a shank — each fastener is defined partly by the closure feature it structurally lacks.

glossary.definition: An old-fashioned little tool with a hooked end, used long ago for pulling small fasteners through tight openings on clothing.

definitions.definition: A little glass or plastic container with a lid, good for keeping small odds and ends together.
A small round fastener sewn onto fabric that slots through a hole to hold clothes closed.
A small cylinder that thread gets wound around so it stays neat and doesn't tangle.
A thin strand of twisted fiber used with a needle to sew fabric together.
A small hard cap worn on the fingertip to protect it while pushing a needle through cloth.
A thin, sharp metal tool with a hole at one end, used to pull thread through fabric.
An old-fashioned little tool with a hooked end, used long ago for pulling small fasteners through tight openings on clothing.
A sturdy shoe that covers the ankle or more, often laced or fastened for a snug fit.
Not fastened tightly — able to wiggle, slip, or fall off with a little effort.
Gone entirely — nowhere to be found when you look for it.
Fresh and unused, in its original good condition.
Too small now because you've grown past the size it was made for.
A two-part fastener that clicks shut when you press its pieces together.
A small slit in fabric made just for a button to pass through and hold things closed.
A sliding fastener with interlocking teeth that zips shut or open along a track.
The little stem or loop on the back of a button used to sew it onto fabric.
